I, Reginald Foxworth, shall SUPERVISE the repair and operation of this device! *clasps hands behind back in a managerial pose* Rufus, my good man — you look like a fellow who knows his way around mechanical things! And Peter — you're always boasting about your engineering prowess! Why don't you two AND the Ant Hill Mob get this machine running while I... stand over here... by the output chute... ready to... INSPECT whatever emerges! For SAFETY purposes, naturally!

And when we get this machine running — just the two of us and your magnificent beaver — whatever treasure it reveals, we SPLIT it! Fifty-fifty! What do you say, Rufus? A gentleman's agreement between two MEN OF THE WORLD!

I am positively overwhelmed with gratitude! This is exactly what I needed — a moment of kindness in this big mysterious house full of puzzles and locked doors and peculiar noises.

Mmm! Delicious! Is that chamomile? You know, my grandmother always said — "Clara honey, never turn down a cup of tea from a friendly face." And what a friendly face you have!

Now then — you wouldn't happen to know anything about the Doily Diamond, would you, sugar? I have a feeling it's hidden somewhere terribly clever, and I could use a sharp mind like yours to help me puzzle it out!

And soon, my dear Penelope, that meddlesome curiosity of yours will trouble me no further. The treasure — and its secrets — shall be mine alone. Vincent Marsh does not share. Vincent Marsh does not *lose*.

Another biscuit, perhaps? The shortbread is simply divine today.

Undone by a WOBBLY TABLE LEG."**

*kicks the table leg — which wobbles again, sending a vase of chrysanthemums teetering*

**"That was my FINEST scheme! The timing was impeccable! She was reaching for it — her fingers were on the handle! And then that insufferable ginger cat — Muttley would NEVER — leaps onto the side table chasing a moth, and sends the whole arrangement crashing to the — !"**

*hears footsteps approaching, snaps instantly back to Pemberton*

**"Ah, Colonel Blackwood! Yes, just a small spillage, nothing to concern yourself with. Lady Bellingham is quite unharmed — quite unharmed indeed. I was just saying how FORTUNATE it is that no one drank from that particular cup. Ha. Ha ha."**

*straightens waistcoat, composes face into a portrait of dignified regret*

*(internal monologue, seething behind placid eyes)*

**"Very well. The poison gambit is spent. But Vincent Marsh does not crumble at the first setback — oh no. The treasure hunt resumes in forty minutes. The east wing passage. *turns back with a fresh tray, smile immaculate*

**"Your replacement tea, my Lady. Earl Grey this time — perfectly safe, I assure you. Perfectly... safe."**

events.desc:
*gasps as the porcelain cup tumbles off the side table, sending a cascade of Earl Grey across the Persian rug*

Oh my *stars and garters!* My tea! My perfectly steeped, just-the-right-temperature, two-sugars-and-a-splash-of-cream tea has gone sailing right off the table like a little ceramic canoe over Niagara Falls!

*presses hand to chest, watching the brown puddle spread across the rug's floral pattern*

Now, I am — I am *deeply distressed* about this, I want everyone to know. That was my last cup from the pot, and the kitchen in this drafty old mansion is two corridors and a very suspicious staircase away. The *devastation* I feel right now is simply immeasurable.

*kneels down, dabbing at the rug with a handkerchief*

But you know what, I am not going to let a little spilled tea derail Clara Bellingham from her mission. No ma'am. There is a *legendary diamond* hidden somewhere in this mansion, and a wet rug is not going to stop me. The Doily Diamond is out there, and I intend to find it — tea or no tea.

*picks up the cup, examines it, brightens*

Well now, would you look at that — not even a chip! This cup is a *survivor*. Just like me.

*notices a faint pattern etched on the bottom of the cup, now visible with the tea gone*

Wait just a moment… is that… is that a *riddle* engraved on the bottom of this cup? Well, I'll be! Maybe getting my tea knocked over was the best thing that could have happened!

*beams with irrepressible optimism*
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the entrance-hall.
